output.summary: An aromatic deciduous shrub native to cool temperate Eurasia and North America, often forming dense colonies from root suckers. Its spring catkins usually occur as male and female flowers on separate plants, though plants may change sex between years. Dried leaves and fruits have seasoned food and beer, and leaves make tea; people who are or may be pregnant should not consume it.
output.edibilityNote: Dried leaves and fruits are used as spice or beer flavouring, and dried leaves as tea; avoid during possible pregnancy.
